result.summary: Changes the default `codeseparator_pos` parameter in test framework helper `TaprootSignatureMsg` to `None` and adds an explicit assertion requiring callers to pass it when `scriptpath=True`. This replaces an invalid default of `-1` that caused an `OverflowError` during unsigned 4-byte serialization.
result.problem: When `scriptpath=True` was used without specifying `codeseparator_pos`, `TaprootSignatureMsg` failed with an `OverflowError` attempting to convert `-1` with `signed=False`. While in-tree tests currently avoid this by passing the argument explicitly, test authors omitting it encountered an obscure Python overflow rather than an explicit assertion.
evidence: Author explanation in PR description: "TaprootSignatureMsg defaults codeseparator_pos to -1 and serializes it with .to_bytes(4, 'little', signed=False), so any scriptpath=True call that relies on the default raises OverflowError."
Commit 81e5c8385b made the integer encoding unsigned while leaving the default as `-1`.
result.changed_since_previous: Instead of changing the default to `0xFFFFFFFF`, the default is now set to `None` and an explicit assertion requires `scriptpath=True` callers to provide the position.
result.card: Updates the test framework helper TaprootSignatureMsg to default codeseparator_pos to None instead of -1 and asserts that script-path callers supply it explicitly. An earlier commit made codeseparator serialization unsigned, which caused scriptpath calls relying on the -1 default to fail with an OverflowError. In-tree tests already specify the parameter explicitly, so this bug did not break existing CI tests.

risk.why: Touches only functional test framework helper code and only enforces an explicit parameter when testing script-path Taproot transactions.
